Zgierz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zgierz, Poland

Demolished. Zgierz's Jewish community grew explosively through the 19th century — from 505 people in 1808 to over 19,000 by 1897 — before contracting to 4,800 by the start of WWII; the Germans transferred most of the community to Głowno in December 1939, and only about 350 survived the war. This cemetery, founded in 1826, held the graves of the town's first two rabbis and other communal leaders before German forces demolished it during the war, removing matzevot to harden roads, felling its trees for building material, and having the site deliberately ploughed under and covered with earth. No tombstones survived that destruction; in 1992, a Canadian descendant of Zgierz's Jews, Jakub Milgrom, funded the cleanup and fencing of a small portion, where a memorial now stands alongside matzevot later recovered by local volunteers.
